messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 4832221111 — p99 latency spike affecting streaming inference; auto-page triggered for oncall. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat. Symptoms: token-level stalls, clients see repeated 503/504s and long tails.

lina (oncall): seeing it in Datadog p99 up to 4.8s on /v1/stream. p95 ~600ms but tail worst. Streaming sessions show chunk delivery gaps. @thomas can you confirm control-plane errors?

thomas (infra): yep, control-plane configfetch is returning 503s to some regions. DB auth token-store is seeing brief 429 bursts. I'm seeing a surge of configfetchs to feature-flag service at 18:03 UTC, likely caused by a rollout.

eva (ml): pattern matches KV cache miss storm — many requests falling back to model cold-starts and prefix cache misses. That amplifies latency. Also noticing increased sequence lengths from a customer test harness.

jonah (sre): grabbing logs. attaching quick grep: ```
2026-03-15T18:02:01Z controlplane: configfetch 503 host=cfg01 shards=3
2026-03-15T18:02:07Z tokenstore: 429 host=auth-db-primaries pool=write
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z gateway: streaming-chunk-timeout trace=abc123
```

maya (support): Customer ticket #12345 reports streaming client rebuffering every 15-30s, affecting a small cohort on eu-west. Only high-throughput customers so far.

lina (oncall): impact: partial degradations for premium customers on eu-west/us-east, estimated 2–5% error rate increase for streaming routes. Not a full outage but SLO p99 breached for streaming. Paging L2/L3? recommend L3 if DB auth remains saturated.

thomas (infra): root cause theory: a feature-flag rollout triggered widespread configfetch invalidations -> control-plane hit to configstore -> configstore falls back to DB -> token-store routing sees extra reads -> auth token throttle -> upstream requests queue -> streaming stalls. Also likely cascading backpressure into inference gateway.

eva (ml): mitigation suggestions: 1) flip feature-flag to previous stable to stop the fanout 2) enable configfetch caching TTL bump 3) serve cached feature flags from edge for 5m 4) temporarily increase auth tokenstore rate window for critical routes. Any cons?

jonah (sre): quick actions in progress: - rolling back FF rollout (in progress) - throttling non-critical endpoints (batch embeddings) to reduce load - enabling emergency configstore cache (edge) TTL=300s - opening a DB read-only pool for configstore to reduce primary contention

thomas (infra): started the rollback at 18:06 UTC — telemetry shows configfetch 503s dropping by ~40% in last 60s. tokenstore 429s still present but trending down.

maya (support): told customer #12345 we're investigating; asked if they can switch to polling fallback; they replied they're seeing steady retries.

eva (ml): enabling model-level fallback: pushing lightweight quantized variant for streaming routes so in-flight sessions can continue with slightly lower quality but much lower latency. Pushed to canary now.

jonah (sre): routing change: route ~20% of traffic for eu-west streaming to dedicated capacity to reduce gateway queues. Doing gradual shift.

lina (oncall): current numbers: p95 620ms, p99 1.9s (was 4.8s). Error rate for streaming down from 5.2% -> 2.1%. Still over SLO for p99 but improving.

thomas (infra): note: controlplane logs still show configfetch spikes tied to a job id `rollout-ff-8472`. Investigating what triggered repeated fetches — looks like client-side revalidation loop due to bad ETag handling in the rollout job.

eva (ml): also saw a KV cache eviction cascade; I'm rehydrating the most common prefixes in the edge caches to cut cold-starts. Doing incremental prefix warmup for top 20 keys.

jonah (sre): decision log: 1) continue FF rollback until no configfetch errors for 3 consecutive mins 2) keep dedicated routing at 20% until queues stable 3) enable emergency TTL 300s for configstore edge caches 4) open ticket with rollout owners to patch ETag logic.

lina (oncall): paging update: not paging to full incident ops yet, keep L2 engaged and page L3 if tokenstore 429s reappear >10/min or p99 >2.5s for 5m.

maya (support): summarizing customer impact for ops duty: affected customers: #12345, #12378; severity moderate; ongoing mitigations applied; warning to CS: possible transient quality drop due to quantized fallback.

thomas (infra): controlplane configfetch 503s nearly gone. tokenstore 429s now rare. DB CPU normalized after opening read-only pool.

eva (ml): model fallback can be turned off after 10 mins of stable p99 <1s; leaving it on until then.

jonah (sre): logs show streaming-chunk gaps reduced to normal cadence. will keep monitoring for tail anomalies. setting a 30m watch.

lina (oncall): handoff to @jordan (next-oncall) at 18:22 UTC. Jordan — summary: brief p99 spike due to FF rollout causing configfetch fanout -> DB/auth tokenstore pressure -> streaming stalls. Rollback in place, edge TTL 300s, dedicated routing 20%, quantized fallback active. Current p99 1.1–1.9s trending down. Continue monitoring, page L3 if regression.

jordan (next-oncall): acknowledged. I have console links? pls post quicklinks.

jonah (sre): quicklinks: https://app.datadog.com/streaming/p99-4832221111, https://console.redwood/configstore/rollout-ff-8472, https://logs.redwood/trace/abc123

jordan (next-oncall): thanks — taking over watch. If anything spikes I'll escalate. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT 4832221111 status CHANGE: mitigated -> watch. auto-page cleared.
